issues.legal_issue: A High Court hearing a second appeal may set aside a factual finding that is perverse and contrary to the evidence on record.
material_facts: The dispute reached the High Court in a second appeal under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The lower appellate court's findings on possession were contrary to the evidence on record and were found to be perverse.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in setting aside the lower appellate court's findings and allowing the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure limits a second appeal to a substantial question of law, but a High Court may set aside subordinate courts' factual findings when they are perverse and contrary to the evidence on record. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.second_appeal: The matter is before the High Court in a second appeal.
predicates.factual_finding_contrary_to_record: A subordinate court made a factual finding that is contrary to the evidence on record.

issues.definition: When a matter is before the High Court in a second appeal and a subordinate court's factual finding is both contrary to the record and perverse, the High Court may set that finding aside.

issues.legal_issue: An unstamped and unregistered sale deed that cannot convey title may be considered to determine the collateral matter of the nature of possession.
material_facts: The parties did not dispute execution of a written sale deed, but it was unstamped and unregistered.
The deed could not convey title, but it recorded the basis on which the purchasers entered possession.
The deed was considered to determine whether the initial possession was illegal or unauthorized.
issues.conclusion: The deed could not convey title, but it could be looked at for the collateral purpose of determining the nature of possession.
issues.legal_principle: A sale deed must be properly stamped and registered to convey title. Even if such a document is inadmissible in evidence for that purpose, it may be considered for a collateral purpose, including the nature of possession. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.civil_land_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute over rights in land.
predicates.instrument_unstamped_or_unregistered: A party relies on a written transfer instrument that is unstamped or unregistered.
predicates.purpose_is_collateral: The instrument is offered to establish a matter collateral to whether it conveyed title, such as the nature of possession.

issues.definition: In a land dispute, an unstamped or unregistered transfer instrument may be considered when it is offered to establish a collateral matter rather than to prove that it conveyed title.

issues.legal_issue: Continuous, uninterrupted possession asserted as hostile to the owner for the required limitation period can establish title by adverse possession.
material_facts: The claimants and their predecessor were in continuous possession from the time they entered under the written transfer until the suit was filed.
The predecessor of the opposing claimants did not dispute the claimants' possession during his lifetime.

The opposing claimants' notice and revenue application acknowledged the claimants' possession, and the revenue proceedings established that possession continued at least through the appeal decided in 1962.
The claimants denied the opposing claimants' title and asserted title to the land in their own right.
The opposing claimants' assertion that they had recovered possession in 1957–58 was contradicted by the revenue proceedings and was found false.
issues.conclusion: The claimants' continuous and uninterrupted possession, coupled with their assertion of hostile title against the opposing claimants, established adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: Adverse possession requires continuous and uninterrupted possession that is hostile to the owner's title and is maintained for the required limitation period. The court relied on the evidence of possession and the parties' assertions of title, including admissions in the notice and the application under Section 58 of the Madhya Bharat Land Revenue and Tenancy Act, 1950. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

rule.if: adverse_possession_suit and possession_continuous_for_limitation_period and possession_uninterrupted and claimant_asserted_hostile_title

predicates.adverse_possession_suit: The proceeding includes a claim to acquire title by adverse possession.
predicates.possession_continuous_for_limitation_per: The claimant or the claimant's predecessor possessed the land continuously for the required limitation period.
predicates.possession_uninterrupted: The claimant's possession was not interrupted during that period.
predicates.claimant_asserted_hostile_title: The claimant asserted a title to the land hostile to the opposing owner's title.

issues.definition: In a claim for adverse possession, continuous and uninterrupted possession for the required period, together with an assertion of hostile title, results in acquisition of title by adverse possession.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot establish a sub-tenancy defense through evidence when the defense was not pleaded and no issue on it was framed.
material_facts: The written statement did not plead the alleged sub-tenancy with material particulars, and no issue on sub-tenancy was framed.
The sub-tenancy argument was advanced at the appellate stage and relied on revenue entries.
The witnesses said to have the best knowledge of the alleged arrangement were not produced to testify.
issues.conclusion: The sub-tenancy argument could not be relied on and was rejected as devoid of merit.
issues.legal_principle: In a civil suit, evidence relating to a matter cannot be considered to build a case that was not pleaded; a properly pleaded matter may be made an issue for determination. The judgment states this as settled law but cites no earlier case.

predicates.civil_suit: The matter is being determined in a civil suit.
predicates.subtenancy_defense_not_pleaded: The party did not plead the alleged sub-tenancy in its written case.
predicates.subtenancy_issue_not_framed: The court did not frame an issue for determination on the alleged sub-tenancy.

issues.definition: In a civil suit, a party cannot rely on an alleged sub-tenancy defense that was neither pleaded nor made an issue for determination.

issues.legal_issue: Possession held by a receiver is not attributable to the opposing claimants when the claimant had already acquired the relevant landholder status before the receiver was appointed.
material_facts: A receiver was appointed over the land in proceedings under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The claimants had become landholders in respect of the land before the receiver was appointed.
issues.conclusion: The receiver's possession could not be treated as possession on behalf of the opposing claimants.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that because the claimants had become landholders before the receiver's appointment, the receiver's possession could not be attributed to the opposing claimants. The proceeding for appointment of the receiver was under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition in the judgment.

predicates.receiver_appointed_in_possession_proceed: A receiver was appointed over the disputed property in a possession-related proceeding.
predicates.claimant_acquired_landholder_status_befo: The claimant acquired the relevant landholder status before the receiver was appointed.

issues.definition: When a receiver is appointed in a possession-related proceeding after the claimant has acquired the relevant landholder status, the receiver's possession is not attributed to the opposing claimants.
